overview:
Ouarzazate sits at a crossroads: the High Atlas to the north, the Draa Valley to the south and the road of the kasbahs to the east. Its clear light, empty landscapes and old fortified villages have made it a favourite of filmmakers, earning it the nickname "Ouallywood". Most travellers only pass through on a desert tour; this private day shows you why it is worth stopping.

You start with the Taourirt Kasbah, the great earthen palace of the Glaoui family, then visit the Atlas Film Studios, where sets from famous films still stand in the desert. In the late morning you drive to Ait Ben Haddou for a guided walk through the most famous ksar in Morocco. After lunch you head east to Skoura, a palm oasis full of kasbahs, including the 17th-century Kasbah Amridil, one of the finest in the south. Most tours sell these as separate trips; we combine all four in one logical loop with short drives.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: about 8 hours
• Start and finish: your hotel or riad in Ouarzazate
• Distance: about 150 km in total, never more than an hour between stops
• Type: private day tour with driver; local guide at Ait Ben Haddou; studio guide at Atlas Studios
• Walking: about 3–4 km, with a 20–30 minute climb in Ait Ben Haddou
• Activity level: easy

WHAT YOU SEE
• Taourirt Kasbah: the 19th-century Glaoui palace, with painted cedar ceilings and carved stucco.
• Atlas Film Studios: sets of ancient Egypt, Rome, Tibet and Jerusalem built in the desert.
• Ait Ben Haddou: the UNESCO-listed ksar on the old caravan route, from the river to the hilltop granary.
• Skoura: a palm grove irrigated by ancient channels, and the Kasbah Amridil with its small museum of daily life.

WHY THIS TOUR WORKS
It brings together the four great sights around Ouarzazate in a logical loop, with short drives and enough time at each stop. The order can be changed to avoid heat or crowds, and lunch is at a terrace restaurant with a view of the ksar.

WHO WILL ENJOY IT
Film fans, history and architecture lovers, families with children (the film sets are a hit) and anyone spending a night or two in Ouarzazate on the way to or from the desert.

WHO MIGHT PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
To continue to the Sahara, take the [2-day Ouarzazate to Merzouga tour](/en-US/morocco/ouarzazate/tours/2-day-tour-from-ouarzazate-to-merzouga-skoura-dades-todra-gorges/5dadd9a9ef01706f9ee87e75). From Marrakech, the [Ait Ben Haddou and Ouarzazate day trip](/en-US/morocco/marrakech/tours/ait-ben-haddou-ouarzazate-day-trip-from-marrakech-over-the-atlas/7c3f043cd0b560a6f555e9c0) covers part of this route.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
Bring a hat, sunscreen and water: there is little shade. Wear shoes with grip for Ait Ben Haddou. Cash in dirhams is useful for entrance fees (kasbahs and studios, each a modest amount), lunch and tips.
descriptions:
What to expect: a loop from Ouarzazate – the kasbah and the film studios in the morning, Ait Ben Haddou at midday and the oasis of Skoura in the afternoon.

Your driver picks you up at your hotel or riad and takes you first to the Taourirt Kasbah in the centre of town. Built in the 19th century and extended by the Glaoui, the powerful lords of the south who controlled the caravan routes over the Atlas, it once housed hundreds of family members, servants and craftsmen. You climb narrow stairs to rooms with painted cedar ceilings, carved stucco and views over the rooftops. Then, on the edge of town, the Atlas Film Studios: opened in 1983 and among the largest in the world by area, they keep sets of an Egyptian temple, a Roman arena, a Tibetan monastery and the streets of Jerusalem, and a studio guide tells you which films were shot here.

In the late morning you drive about 30 km to Ait Ben Haddou. With a local guide you cross the Ounila river and climb through the lanes of the ksar – earthen houses, towers and a mosque stacked on the hill – to the old communal granary at the top, where the view stretches over the valley and the caravan route. Lunch is at a terrace restaurant facing the ksar. In the afternoon you drive back through Ouarzazate and east to Skoura, where palm, olive and fruit trees grow along ancient irrigation channels. The 17th-century Kasbah Amridil, still owned by the same family, has a small museum of daily life with an olive press, a bread oven and old tools; it appears on the old 50-dirham banknote. You are back in Ouarzazate around 17:00.

SCHEDULE (times are estimates)
08:30 – Pick-up at your hotel or riad.
08:45 – Taourirt Kasbah (about 45 min).
09:45 – Atlas Film Studios: guided visit (about 1 hour).
11:15 – Ait Ben Haddou: guided walk to the granary (about 1.5 hours).
13:00 – Lunch near Ait Ben Haddou (about 1 hour, not included).
14:30 – Drive back through Ouarzazate to Skoura (about 1 hour).
15:30 – Skoura palm grove and Kasbah Amridil (about 1 hour).
17:00 – Drop-off in Ouarzazate.

GOOD TO KNOW
• The film studios occasionally close for shoots; we then visit the smaller CLA Studios or the Cinema Museum.
• Ait Ben Haddou is free to enter, but some families charge a small fee to visit their houses.
• Kasbah Amridil is privately owned and charges a small entrance fee.

INCLUDED: private vehicle and driver, local guide at Ait Ben Haddou, bottled water.
NOT INCLUDED: entrance fees, lunch, drinks, tips.

IF THE WEATHER TURNS: summer afternoons are very hot; the order can change so that outdoor visits happen early. In rare rain, the earthen kasbahs are fragile: paths may be closed and the studios become the main visit.

WHAT YOU'LL TASTE
A Berber omelette cooked in a tagine dish, a lamb tagine with almonds and prunes, or a kefta tagine with eggs. In Skoura, dates from the palm grove and, in spring, rose products from the nearby Valley of Roses.

PHOTO SPOTS
• The towers of Taourirt from the street outside.
• The Egyptian temple set at the studios.
• Ait Ben Haddou from the opposite bank of the river.
• Kasbah Amridil framed by palm trees.

ACCESSIBILITY
The kasbahs have steep stairs and dark rooms. Ait Ben Haddou can be enjoyed from the river bank if the climb is too hard. The studios are flat.

WHAT YOU TAKE AWAY: the architecture of the south, the magic of cinema and the green calm of an oasis.

faq.question: Where does the tour start?
faq.answer: At your hotel or riad in Ouarzazate, at around 08:30. We can also pick you up in Ait Ben Haddou or Skoura if you are staying there.

faq.question: Are entrance fees included?
faq.answer: No. The Taourirt Kasbah, the Atlas Film Studios and the Kasbah Amridil each charge a modest entrance fee, paid on the spot in dirhams. Ait Ben Haddou itself is free.

faq.question: Is a guide included?
faq.answer: Yes. A local guide accompanies you at Ait Ben Haddou, and the Atlas Studios have their own guides included in the ticket. Your driver explains the other stops.

faq.question: Is lunch included?
faq.answer: No. Your driver suggests a terrace restaurant facing Ait Ben Haddou, where a tagine lunch costs a modest amount. Vegetarian food is easy to find.

faq.question: Is it private?
faq.answer: Yes. The vehicle, driver and guide are only for your group, so you can change the order, stay longer at a stop or skip one.

faq.question: Can children join?
faq.answer: Yes. Children love the film sets and exploring the kasbahs. The climb at Ait Ben Haddou is short but steep, so hold small hands on the stairs.

faq.question: Which films were shot here?
faq.answer: Ait Ben Haddou and the studios have appeared in many productions, including Lawrence of Arabia, Gladiator, Kingdom of Heaven and Game of Thrones. The studio guide shows you the sets and tells the stories behind them.

faq.question: What is the Kasbah Taourirt?
faq.answer: A 19th-century earthen palace built by the Glaoui family, who controlled the trade routes of the south. It was once home to hundreds of people and is partly restored, with painted ceilings and stucco in some rooms.

faq.question: What if the studios are closed for filming?
faq.answer: It happens occasionally. We then visit the CLA Studios or the Cinema Museum in Ouarzazate instead, so you still see real film sets and props.

faq.question: When is the best time?
faq.answer: October to April has pleasant temperatures. In summer it is very hot by midday, so we start earlier and change the order to keep outdoor visits for the morning.

faq.question: How much walking is there?
faq.answer: About 3–4 km in total. The only real climb is the 20–30 minute walk up to the granary at Ait Ben Haddou; the rest is flat or on stairs inside the kasbahs.

faq.question: Can I start from Marrakech?
faq.answer: Yes, but it makes a long day of about 12 hours with the drive over the Atlas. See our Ait Ben Haddou and Ouarzazate day trip from Marrakech, or spend a night in Ouarzazate and do this tour the next day.

faq.question: Can we add the Draa Valley or the Valley of Roses?
faq.answer: Yes. As a private tour it can be extended to the Valley of Roses (Kelaat M'Gouna) or south over the Tizi n'Tinifift pass to the Draa Valley and Agdz. Ask us for the timing and price.
